Subject: AWS multi-product listing — landing copy + field navigation

Team — attaching v3 of the landing copy and the hero image for the StratusTech bundle we want to publish next week (attachments: redwood_aws_landing_v3.docx, hero_2.png). Goal is to get the listing live and ensure field reps have a clean navigation script so they can demo quickly.

Quick asks: 
- Can you review the hero headline + 3 benefit bullets — we need something that reads well on the AWS product tile and in the one-line.
- Field navigation: I added a 1-page cheatsheet (draft) describing which SKU to show for a pricing/POC question. Tessa / Rafael, please validate SKU flow and entitlements.
- Any regulatory or claim flags (Kimberly) we should avoid calling out?

Timeline: want final copy by EOD Monday so legal can kick off private offer paperwork.

Thanks — Connor

Connor — quick read through, inline notes below. I left page comments in the doc too, but calling out the priority items here: 

1) Hero headline: current "Industry-grade LLM inference at predictable economics" reads okay but is a bit long for the AWS tile. Suggest: "High-performance LLM inference — predictable cost, enterprise SLA" (shorter, keeps SLA promise).

2) Benefit bullets: remove any absolute claims like "cheapest" or "near-zero latency". Replace with measurable language: "Optimized for sub-100ms p50 on typical web workloads (see benchmarks)" and "Configurable reserved capacity and private deployment options".

3) Security blurb: add one sentence about SOC 2 + optional customer-owned KMS — customer-facing copy should not mention internal implementation details. I'll flag suggested wording in the doc.

4) Field nav cheatsheet: Rafael/Tessa — confirm the SKU names map to the product tiles (we don't want mismatched SKU names in the buy flow). Also add a quick troubleshooting line for trial entitlements.

I'll be available for a 30min sync tomorrow AM if you want to go line-by-line.

Kimberly Park
Head of Marketplace Compliance | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS multi-product listing — landing copy + field navigation

Thanks Connor — I rewrote the hero & the three bullets in the attached doc (redwood_aws_landing_v3.docx). Paste of the proposed hero block below for quick reference: 

Headline: High-performance LLM inference — predictable cost and enterprise controls
Subhead (one-line for catalog): Optimized GPU serving with reserved capacity, private deployment, and built-in observability.
Bullets (short):
• Predictable per-token economics with intelligent batching and caching
• Enterprise controls: private deployment, customer KMS, audit logs
• SLA-backed dedicated pools and automatic fallbacks to keep features live

I also trimmed the technical claims and added a "How to demo" blur that the field team can use: two clicks to start a trial, show the reserved capacity SKU, then switch to hosted to illustrate failover. That is included in field-nav-cheatsheet.pdf (attached).

Two open asks for Rafael/Tessa:
- Confirm the SKU labels in field-nav-cheatsheet.pdf map to the catalog SKUs we will create (names are placeholders right now).
- Rafael: can you confirm the burst-to-hosted fallback behavior and wording? I added a short sentence but want accurate phrasing.

If this looks good I'll finalize for legal and the AWS private offer.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Marketing Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Jane — forwarding the updated copy and the field nav cheatsheet for StratusTech. AWS ops, could you confirm two quick implementation points so we can schedule the private offer sign-off?

1) Hero image sizing: we are attaching hero_2.png (1200x628). Does that meet the current AWS catalog spec for the product tile? If not, please confirm target size and max file size.
2) SKU mapping: Marissa noted the SKU names in the cheatsheet are placeholders. Can AWS ops confirm any reserved naming constraints or recommendations for multi-product bundles so the field team can reference the exact SKU in demos?

Quick context: this bundle targets regulated analytics customers; Kimberly has trimmed claims and added SOC 2 / KMS language. We want to go live to support the upcoming StratusTech POC next month.
